parsed.attack: The product is unshareable by construction: the wedge is explicitly 'only this plot's own beds and nothing about anyone else's garden', so there is no artifact, no invite and no social object that can travel - nothing in my Sunday briefing is legible or useful to the plot holder next to me. That leaves the stated channel carrying everything, and allotment associations are volunteer-run, commercially wary, and reach 60-150 plot holders via a monthly newsletter or a physical noticeboard, so 1,000 subscribers means roughly 30 separately negotiated relationships on a monthly cycle into a total UK plot population near 330,000: linear founder-hours with no compounding. Their own kill line asks for 10 associations in 12 weeks, which is a sales quota, and at $4 a month with paid acquisition costing $20-$80 per payer there is no way to buy the rest.
parsed.strongest_defence: Allotment culture is unusually chatty and physically co-located - people talk over the fence every weekend, the fastest cycle time available to any of these ideas - and the briefing does throw off a boast-shaped line ('it reminded me I sowed these three weeks too late last year') that travels in the tens-of-thousands-strong UK allotment Facebook groups at no cost.
parsed.verdict_reason: The briefing is deliberately private and so carries no shareable unit, leaving about 30 hand-sold noticeboard relationships on a monthly cycle as the only stated channel.
